(c) rule_types: '[.rules[].type] | sort | join(",")' — sort makes comparison order-independent; alphabetical sort of deletion/non_fast_forward/update produces 'd,n,u' ordering; expected literal matches. Null .rules yields empty join string != expected literal — no false-positive. If GitHub API ever adds implicit rule types the join would differ and the check would fail (over-strict, not under-strict). (d) include_match: '.conditions.ref_name.include | index($pattern) // -1' — jq // operator is null/false-only, not triggered by integer 0; pattern at position 0 returns '0' != '-1' → verification passes correctly. Null chain propagation through .conditions.ref_name.include → null | index → null // -1 → '-1' → exits correctly. (e) exclude_count: '.conditions.ref_name.exclude | length' — null|length=0 in jq; empty-array|length=0; both allow verification to pass, which is correct. (f) bypass_count: '.bypass_actors | length' — same null/empty analysis as (e), correct. All six error messages include ruleset id and actual vs expected values. Assertion order (target first, enforcement second, rules third, include fourth, exclude fifth, bypass sixth) is logical for defence-in-depth. No jq syntax errors found.

r4_additional_verifications.check: (2) Probe: POST-response ID capture — gh api -X POST response shape, jq -r '.id' on success/error paths
r4_additional_verifications.detail: lines 93–101: local create_response declared on separate line from its assignment — set -e will fire on the assignment if gh api exits non-zero (bash local-declaration-vs-assignment separation is correct; local on same line as assignment would mask exit code). On gh api success (HTTP 2xx), GitHub's Ruleset API returns the created ruleset JSON including integer .id field; jq -r '.id' outputs the integer as a string. Guard '[ -z "$final_id" ] || [ "$final_id" = "null" ]' covers (a) empty string (gh api returned empty body) and (b) jq null (API returned JSON without .id field). On gh api failure (non-2xx), set -euo pipefail exits before the jq line — the guard is never reached but is correct defence-in-depth for the edge case where gh api exits 0 with an unexpected body. Non-JSON gh api responses would cause jq to exit non-zero, which set -e would catch. No new correctness gap.

r4_additional_verifications.check: (4) Probe: git rev-parse --show-toplevel portability on fresh checkout
r4_additional_verifications.detail: DISPATCH-NOTE.md post-merge sequence (lines 79–92): 'cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"'. git rev-parse --show-toplevel outputs the absolute path of the top-level working tree directory and works from any subdirectory of a git checkout, including the root itself. On a fresh clone of the SCP repo, the operator may be at any depth (e.g., in docs/, scripts/, or the root). The command correctly resolves the top-level in all these cases. Prerequisite note in the block (lines 70–76) tells the operator to have gh authenticated and admin scope before running. The only failure mode is the operator not being inside any git checkout, which produces a clear 'fatal: not a git repository' message. Correct and portable fix for NEW-R3-SAFE-005.

structured_review.summary: R4 correctness review of 020F post fix-round-3. COR-R3-001 confirmed closed: branch-protection.md 'How to apply' section now says 'Three idempotent appliers', configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh is in the apply block, env-var overrides for 020F are documented, and the centralised verify block has the renovate/v* ruleset command. POST-response ID capture is correct: local declaration and assignment on separate lines preserves set -e semantics; null/.id guard handles unexpected API shapes. final_id is set in both branches before the verification block. git rev-parse --show-toplevel is correctly portable. FIX-ROUND-3.md verdicts table matches R3 JSON findings exactly. STATUS.md quarterly-review row correctly enumerates all three rulesets. The fix was applied to FIX-ROUND-2.md's enumeration rather than to DISPATCH-NOTE.md itself. Fix: add 'Reference: docs/DECISIONS.md D-034.' to DISPATCH-NOTE.md's Tag series section (line ~118). No implementation correctness regressions introduced by fix-round-3. Verdict: PASS.
